<b>Нуклеотид</b> = азотистое основание +: Nucleotide = nitrogenous base + pentose + phosphate (left: AMP). Bases: purines (adenine, guanine — two rings) and pyrimidines (cytosine, thymine, uracil — one ring; right). DNA contains deoxyribose and thymine, RNA contains ribose and uracil. In the center is adenine, with its atoms colored by their origin in purine ring synthesis: glycine (C4, C5, N7), aspartate (N1 and the amino group), glutamine (N3, N9), CO₂ (C6), formyl-THF, a folic acid derivative (C2, C8). The ring is assembled directly on ribose 5-phosphate (from PRPP).
<b>Распад пуринов.</b> АМФ → ИМФ → инози: Purine breakdown. AMP → IMP → inosine → hypoxanthine → xanthine → uric acid; guanine also yields xanthine. The last two reactions are catalyzed by xanthine oxidase (molybdenum, FAD). In humans uric acid is the end product, and it is poorly soluble. In excess (heredity, meat and beer, kidney failure) its sodium salt precipitates as needle-shaped crystals in the joints — gout, with attacks most often in the big toe — and forms kidney stones. Turn on allopurinol, a hypoxanthine analog that inhibits xanthine oxidase: less uric acid is formed and the crystals dissolve.
<b>Синтез нуклеотидов и антиметаболиты.<: Nucleotide synthesis and antimetabolites. The cell builds purines and pyrimidines from amino acids, CO₂ and ribose, and transferring one-carbon groups requires tetrahydrofolic acid, which is regenerated by dihydrofolate reductase (real structure with the coenzyme NADPH, PDB 1RX1). Rapidly dividing cells depend on this pathway especially heavily, and chemotherapy exploits this: methotrexate, a folate analog, binds tightly to DHFR; 5-fluorouracil (right, next to thymine), a thymine analog, blocks thymidylate synthase. Some bases are not synthesized anew but recycled via the “salvage pathway” through the enzyme HGPRT; its inherited deficiency is Lesch–Nyhan syndrome (gout and self-injury in boys).
аденин: откуда атомы: adenine: where the atoms come from
Из чего строятся буквы генетического код: What the letters of the genetic code are built from, what they turn into when broken down, and why excess uric acid ends up as joint pain.
\n <div><h2>Обмен нуклеотидов</h2>\:
Nucleotide metabolism

Dietary nucleoproteins are broken down: in the stomach into proteins and nucleic acids; in the intestine pancreatic DNases and RNases and phosphodiesterases yield nucleotides, and nucleotidases yield nucleosides, which are what gets absorbed. But to synthesize its own nucleic acids the body makes nucleotides almost entirely by itself.

Pyrimidines

The pyrimidine ring is built from carbamoyl phosphate (cytosolic CPS II) and aspartate, and ribose is attached at the end (via orotic acid). Pyrimidines are broken down to soluble β-alanine, CO₂ and NH₃ — which is why pyrimidines have no storage diseases like gout. Hereditary orotic aciduria is a defect in UMP synthesis.

Deoxyribonucleotides

They are formed from ribonucleotides by ribonucleotide reductase (inhibited by the anticancer drug hydroxyurea); the thymidine nucleotide is made by thymidylate synthase with methylene-THF.

\n <div><h2>Два пути сигнала</h2>\n:
Two signaling routes

Hydrophilic hormones (proteins, peptides, catecholamines) act through membrane receptors: ionotropic (channels), metabotropic (via G proteins: Gs activates adenylyl cyclase, Gi inhibits it, Gq activates phospholipase C → IP₃ and Ca²⁺ + DAG), and enzyme receptors (tyrosine kinases, guanylyl cyclase). Second messengers: cAMP, cGMP, Ca²⁺, IP₃, DAG, NO. The response takes seconds to minutes and changes enzyme activity.

Lipophilic hormones (steroids, iodothyronines, calcitriol) enter the cell and act on genes through intracellular receptors: the response takes hours and changes the amount of enzymes.

Hierarchy

Hypothalamus (releasing and inhibiting hormones) → pituitary (tropic hormones: ACTH, TSH, FSH, LH, GH, prolactin) → peripheral glands. Negative feedback: the hormones of the glands inhibit the hypothalamus and pituitary.

<b>Абсорбтивный период</b> (0–4 ч после: Absorptive state (0–4 h after a meal). Glucose and amino acids travel from the gut into the portal vein, fats in chylomicrons. Insulin is high: the liver stores glycogen and converts excess glucose into fat (VLDL → adipose tissue), muscles take up glucose (GLUT4) and build glycogen and protein, and adipose tissue stores TAG. The brain runs on glucose.
<b>Постабсорбтивный период.</b> Инсулин: Postabsorptive state. Insulin falls and glucagon rises. The liver breaks down glycogen and releases glucose — above all for the brain and red blood cells. Adipose tissue begins lipolysis: fatty acids fuel muscle and the heart. Gluconeogenesis from lactate (Cori cycle), alanine and glycerol gains momentum.
<b>Ранний голод.</b> Гликоген печени исч: Early starvation. Liver glycogen is exhausted (within ~24 h). Glucose comes from gluconeogenesis, mainly from amino acids of muscle protein (cortisol) and glycerol. Fatty acids are the main fuel of almost all tissues; the liver turns their excess into ketone bodies, whose level rises rapidly.
<b>Длительный голод.</b> Мозг перестраив: Prolonged starvation. The brain adapts and covers up to 2/3 of its needs with ketone bodies — glucose use, and with it protein breakdown, drops sharply: the body spares protein. The kidneys also make glucose. Fat lasts 1–2 months (in a person of normal weight); death comes when vital proteins start to be broken down.
<b>Мозг</b> тратит ~20% энергии покоя, о: The brain uses ~20% of resting energy, about 120 g of glucose a day, and cannot use fatty acids (they do not cross the blood–brain barrier). In starvation it switches to ketone bodies.
<b>Печень</b> — распределительный центр:: The liver is the distribution center: it stores and releases glucose (glycogen, gluconeogenesis), makes VLDL and ketone bodies, and converts amino acids into urea. In starvation it runs on fatty acids itself.
<b>Кишечник</b> всасывает продукты перев: The intestine absorbs the products of digestion; its own cells feed mainly on glutamine.
<b>Жировая ткань</b> — главное хранилище: Adipose tissue is the main energy store (TAG). Insulin makes it store; glucagon and epinephrine make it release fatty acids and glycerol. It is also an endocrine organ (leptin, adiponectin).
<b>Мышцы</b> — 40% массы тела. После еды: Muscles make up 40% of body mass. After a meal they store glycogen and build protein; at rest and in starvation they run on fatty acids and ketones; in prolonged starvation their protein is a reserve of amino acids for gluconeogenesis.
<b>Почки</b> при длительном голоде синте: The kidneys, in prolonged starvation, synthesize up to half of the glucose and excrete ammonia, compensating for the acidity of ketone bodies.
<b>Сердце</b> предпочитает жирные кислот: The heart prefers fatty acids (up to 70% of its energy) and readily uses lactate and ketone bodies.
Органы делят топливо как слаженная коман: Organs share fuel like a well-coordinated team: after a meal they store it, when fasting they share it, and in starvation they adapt so that the brain is never left without food.
\n <div><h2>Регуляция</h2>\n:
Regulation

The key pair is insulin (the anabolic hormone of the fed state) and glucagon (the catabolic hormone of fasting); their ratio sets the direction of metabolism in the liver. They are assisted by epinephrine (a fast signal of stress and exertion), cortisol (gluconeogenesis from protein during prolonged fasting and stress), growth hormone and thyroid hormones.

Numbers

  • Adult stores: glycogen ~400–500 g (≈2000 kcal), fat ~10–15 kg (≈100,000 kcal), muscle protein ~6 kg (only partly usable).
  • Fasting blood sugar is 3.3–5.5 mmol/L and stays around 3.5 even on day 40 of starvation.

Diabetes mellitus

It resembles “starvation amid plenty”: without enough insulin, cells do not get glucose, the liver keeps producing it, and lipolysis and ketogenesis switch on as in starvation — yet blood sugar is high.

<b>Гемоглобин</b> (реальная структура PD: Hemoglobin (real structure PDB 4HHB): 2 α chains (light blue) and 2 β chains (pink), each with a heme carrying an Fe²⁺ ion that reversibly binds O₂. Binding is cooperative: the first O₂ molecule binds with difficulty but changes the protein’s shape (the transition from the tense T state to the relaxed R state — the chain pairs rotate by ~15°), and each subsequent one binds more easily. That is why the saturation curve is S-shaped: in the lungs (pO₂ ≈ 100) Hb becomes almost fully saturated, while in tissues (≈ 40) and working muscles (≈ 20) it releases a lot of oxygen. Move pO₂ and turn on the factors.
<b>Гем</b> — плоское порфириновое кольцо: Heme is a flat porphyrin ring with an iron ion in the center (real coordinates of oxyhemoglobin 1GZX: you can see that O₂ is bound at an angle). The iron is bonded to the 4 nitrogen atoms of the ring, its fifth bond goes to the protein’s proximal histidine F8, and the sixth position is for O₂. The distal histidine E7 (the second one) stabilizes O₂ with a hydrogen bond and hinders CO. The iron must be ferrous: oxidized Fe³⁺ gives methemoglobin, which does not carry oxygen (poisoning with nitrites and some drugs). Carbon monoxide binds heme 200–250 times more tightly than oxygen — CO poisoning is dangerous even at low concentrations.
<b>Серповидноклеточная анемия</b> — клас: Sickle cell anemia is the classic “molecular disease” (L. Pauling, 1949). A single substitution in the β-chain gene: glutamic acid → valine at position 6 (HbS). In the deoxy form, the hydrophobic valine on the molecule’s surface sticks to a neighboring hemoglobin — the molecules polymerize into long rigid fibers (14-stranded filaments), and the red blood cell deforms into a “sickle”. Such cells block capillaries (pain, organ infarcts) and are rapidly destroyed (anemia). Carriers of a single HbS allele (sickle cell trait) are more resistant to falciparum malaria — which is why the allele is common in Africa.
<b>Эффект Бора.</b> В работающих тканях: Bohr effect. Working tissues have a lot of CO₂ and H⁺: protons bind to hemoglobin and stabilize the T state — O₂ affinity falls, the curve shifts to the right, and oxygen is released exactly where it is needed most. In the lungs the reverse happens.
<b>2,3-Бисфосфоглицерат</b> (из гликолиз: 2,3-Bisphosphoglycerate (from red cell glycolysis) binds in the central cavity between the β chains of deoxyhemoglobin and lowers O₂ affinity. Its level rises at high altitude and in anemia, so tissues receive more oxygen.
<b>Фетальный гемоглобин</b> (α₂γ₂) плохо: Fetal hemoglobin (α₂γ₂) binds 2,3-BPG poorly, so its curve lies further left — the fetus takes oxygen from the mother’s blood across the placenta.
<b>Отравление CO.</b> Карбоксигемоглобин: CO poisoning. Carboxyhemoglobin does not carry O₂ (here half of the hemes are occupied), and the remaining hemes hold oxygen more tightly (the curve shifts left) — a double blow to oxygen delivery. Treatment is pure oxygen, and in severe cases a hyperbaric chamber.
<b>Миоглобин</b> мышц — одна цепь, один: Muscle myoglobin has one chain and one heme and no cooperativity: its curve is hyperbolic and its affinity very high. It takes O₂ from hemoglobin and releases it to the mitochondria only during intense exertion.
Около 270 миллионов молекул гемоглобина: About 270 million hemoglobin molecules in every red blood cell. How this protein picks up oxygen in the lungs and releases it to the tissues right when they need it.
\n <div><h2>Гемоглобин</h2>\n:
Hemoglobin

A chromoprotein: the protein globin + 4 hemes. Normal range: 130–160 g/L in men, 120–140 g/L in women. Forms: HbA (α₂β₂, 97%), HbA₂ (α₂δ₂), fetal HbF (α₂γ₂). Derivatives: oxyhemoglobin, deoxyhemoglobin, carbaminohemoglobin (CO₂ on amino groups), carboxyhemoglobin (CO), methemoglobin (Fe³⁺), glycated HbA1c (reflects average blood sugar over 2–3 months in diabetes).

CO₂ transport

About 10% of CO₂ is carried in the blood as carbaminohemoglobin, the rest as bicarbonate: red cell carbonic anhydrase converts CO₂ + H₂O into H₂CO₃ → H⁺ + HCO₃⁻; the H⁺ is taken up by hemoglobin (a buffer).

Hemoglobinopathies

Qualitative (HbS and hundreds of other mutant hemoglobins) and quantitative — thalassemias (reduced synthesis of α or β chains).

<b>Синтез гема</b> идёт во всех клетках,: Heme synthesis takes place in all cells, most of all in the bone marrow (for hemoglobin) and the liver (for cytochromes P450). The pathway begins and ends in the mitochondrion: glycine + succinyl-CoA → 5-aminolevulinic acid (enzyme ALA synthase, coenzyme vitamin B₆; this is the key regulated step). Two ALA molecules form the pyrrole porphobilinogen, and four pyrroles close into a ring — a porphyrinogen; after decarboxylations and oxidation this gives protoporphyrin IX, into which ferrochelatase inserts Fe²⁺. Turn on the disorders: a block in the pathway leads to a buildup of precursors.
<b>Распад гема.</b> Эритроцит живёт окол: Heme breakdown. A red blood cell lives about 120 days; ~6 g of hemoglobin is destroyed each day, yielding ~250–300 mg of bilirubin. In macrophages of the spleen and liver, heme oxygenase opens the heme ring (O₂ and NADPH are required), releasing CO (the only endogenous source of carbon monoxide) and iron, which is reused. The product is green biliverdin (the color of an “old” bruise), which biliverdin reductase reduces to orange bilirubin — insoluble in water and toxic to the brain. In the liver, UDP-glucuronosyltransferase attaches two glucuronic acids to it, and the water-soluble bilirubin diglucuronide (“direct”) is excreted in bile.
<b>Путь билирубина.</b> «Непрямой» (своб: The bilirubin pathway. “Indirect” (free) bilirubin from the spleen is carried in the blood by albumin. The liver takes it up, conjugates it and excretes it in bile into the gut. There bacteria convert it into urobilinogen; most of it becomes stercobilin, which colors stool brown; a little urobilinogen is absorbed, and part of it reaches the urine (urobilin gives urine its yellow color). If any link fails, bilirubin builds up in the blood and stains the skin and sclerae — jaundice (visible when bilirubin exceeds ~35 µmol/L). Choose a type of jaundice; click an organ for details.
<b>Отравление свинцом.</b> Свинец блокир: Lead poisoning. Lead blocks the SH groups of ALA dehydratase and ferrochelatase: ALA rises in blood and urine, and protoporphyrin accumulates in red blood cells (zinc enters the ring instead of iron). Heme and hemoglobin are left unfinished — anemia with basophilic stippling of red cells — and excess ALA is toxic to the nervous system.
<b>Острая перемежающаяся порфирия</b> —: Acute intermittent porphyria is an inherited deficiency of PBG deaminase. Porphyrins do not accumulate (the skin is spared), but ALA and porphobilinogen do, and they are neurotoxic: attacks of severe abdominal pain, psychiatric and neurological disturbances. The urine darkens in light. Attacks are triggered by drugs that induce P450 (barbiturates), alcohol and fasting — anything that increases the synthesis of ALA synthase. Treatment is hemin and glucose (they suppress ALA synthase).
<b>Поздняя кожная порфирия</b> — самая ч: Porphyria cutanea tarda is the most common porphyria: the activity of uroporphyrinogen decarboxylase is reduced (often because of alcohol, hepatitis C or iron overload). Porphyrins accumulate — they fluoresce and absorb light, generating reactive oxygen species: blisters, scars and fragility of sun-exposed skin. The urine is pinkish-red.
<b>Печень</b>: захват билирубина (белки-: Liver: uptake of bilirubin (ligandin carrier proteins), conjugation with glucuronic acid (UDP-glucuronosyltransferase in the ER), and active export into bile (the MRP2 transporter — the slowest step). Gilbert’s syndrome is a genetically reduced conjugation in ~5% of people: a harmless mild jaundice during fasting and stress.
<b>Селезёнка</b> — «кладбище» эритроцито: Spleen — the “graveyard” of red blood cells: its macrophages engulf old and damaged cells and break down hemoglobin: globin into amino acids, iron onto ferritin and transferrin, heme into bilirubin.
<b>Желчный пузырь</b> копит и концентрир: The gallbladder stores and concentrates bile. A stone or tumor blocking the bile duct causes obstructive jaundice.
<b>Кишечник</b>: бактерии отщепляют глюк: Intestine: bacteria remove glucuronic acid and reduce bilirubin to urobilinogens and then to stercobilin. In newborns the gut is still sterile.
<b>Почки</b> фильтруют только растворимы: The kidneys filter only soluble substances: free bilirubin is bound to albumin and does not enter the urine, whereas direct (conjugated) bilirubin does and makes the urine dark.
<b>Моча</b> окрашена уробилином. Билируб: Urine is colored by urobilin. Bilirubin in the urine is always a sign of elevated direct bilirubin in the blood (hepatic or obstructive jaundice).
<b>Гемолитическая (надпечёночная) желтух: Hemolytic (prehepatic) jaundice: red blood cells are destroyed too quickly (hereditary anemias, Rh incompatibility, malaria, poisons). The liver cannot conjugate all the bilirubin in time, so indirect bilirubin rises. Bile carries more bilirubin — stool and urine are dark from excess stercobilin and urobilin; there is no bilirubin in the urine.
<b>Печёночная (паренхиматозная) желтуха<: Hepatic (hepatocellular) jaundice: hepatitis, cirrhosis, poisoning. Damaged hepatocytes take up and conjugate bilirubin less well and “leak” — both forms rise in the blood, especially direct bilirubin; it passes into the urine (beer-colored urine), and stool is lighter. ALT and AST rise in the blood.
<b>Механическая (подпечёночная) желтуха<: Obstructive (posthepatic) jaundice: bile cannot reach the gut (a stone in the duct, a tumor of the pancreatic head). Conjugated bilirubin returns to the blood — direct bilirubin rises sharply, urine is dark, stool is pale, there is no urobilin in the urine; the skin itches because of bile acids.
<b>Физиологическая желтуха новорождённых: Physiological jaundice of the newborn (days 2–5): after birth fetal hemoglobin is destroyed, while the liver’s UDP-glucuronosyltransferase is still immature — indirect bilirubin rises. The danger is kernicterus (indirect bilirubin enters the brain). Treatment is phototherapy: blue light (~460 nm) converts bilirubin into water-soluble isomers that are excreted without conjugation.
<b>Обратная связь.</b> Гем (и гемин-преп: Feedback. Heme (and the drug hemin) suppresses both the synthesis and the activity of ALA synthase — flux through the pathway drops sharply. Conversely, drugs that demand a lot of cytochrome P450 (barbiturates, some anticonvulsants) increase the synthesis of ALA synthase in the liver — in patients with porphyria this triggers an attack.
<b>Фототерапия желтухи новорождённых.</b: Phototherapy for neonatal jaundice. Blue light (~460 nm) is absorbed by bilirubin in the skin and converts it into photoisomers (Z,E isomers and lumirubin): the intramolecular hydrogen bonds break, and the molecule becomes soluble and is excreted in bile and urine without conjugation.
Как клетка собирает гем из глицина и сук: How the cell assembles heme from glycine and succinyl-CoA — and what it turns into once a red blood cell has served its 120 days.
\n <div><h2>Нормы</h2><ul><li>Общий:
Normal values

  • Total serum bilirubin 8.5–20.5 µmol/L; of this, indirect (free) ~75%, direct (conjugated) ~25%.
  • Jaundice becomes visible when bilirubin exceeds ~30–35 µmol/L.

Differential diagnosis of jaundice

  • Hemolytic: ↑ indirect; urine — ↑ urobilin, no bilirubin; stool dark.
  • Hepatic: ↑ direct and indirect; urine — bilirubin and urobilin; stool lighter; ↑ ALT, AST.
  • Obstructive: ↑↑ direct; urine — bilirubin, no urobilin; stool acholic; ↑ alkaline phosphatase, cholesterol, bile acids.

Inherited hyperbilirubinemias

Gilbert (reduced conjugation, mild), Crigler–Najjar (almost no UDP-glucuronosyltransferase, severe), Dubin–Johnson and Rotor (impaired excretion of direct bilirubin).

<b>pH крови</b> держится в узких предела: Blood pH is kept within the narrow range 7.35–7.45; below it is acidosis, above it alkalosis. The main plasma buffer is bicarbonate: CO₂ + H₂O ⇌ H₂CO₃ ⇌ H⁺ + HCO₃⁻ (in red blood cells the reaction is sped up by carbonic anhydrase). Its strength is that both parts are regulated: CO₂ is exhaled by the lungs (within minutes), and HCO₃⁻ is retained or excreted by the kidneys (over days). pH is set by their ratio: pH = 6.1 + log([HCO₃⁻] / 0.03·pCO₂); normally 24 mmol/L to 40 mmHg, i.e. 20 : 1. Other buffers are hemoglobin, protein and phosphate.
<b>Белки плазмы</b>: 65–85 г/л. При <b>э: Plasma proteins: 65–85 g/L. In electrophoresis on paper or in a gel, proteins move in an electric field toward the anode (+) at different speeds and separate into 5 fractions: albumins (55–65%) maintain oncotic pressure (keep water in the vessels) and carry fatty acids, bilirubin, hormones and drugs; α₁ (antitrypsin, HDL), α₂ (haptoglobin, ceruloplasmin, macroglobulin), β (iron-carrying transferrin, LDL, complement components), and γ-globulins — antibodies (real structure of IgG, PDB 1IGY).
<b>Свёртывание крови</b> — каскад протео: Blood clotting is a proteolytic cascade: each activated factor (a serine protease) activates many molecules of the next one, so the signal is amplified thousands of times. The extrinsic pathway is triggered by tissue factor from the damaged wall (VIIa), the intrinsic pathway by contact with collagen (XII → XI → IX + VIII). Both converge on factor Xa (real structure 1IQJ), which together with Va converts prothrombin into thrombin. Thrombin cleaves fibrinogen — fibrin strands weave into a mesh that reinforces the platelet plug and traps red blood cells. Thrombin accelerates the cascade by positive feedback (red arrow).
<b>Дыхательный ацидоз</b>: CO₂ копится и: Respiratory acidosis: CO₂ builds up because of poor ventilation (COPD, depression of the respiratory center by opioids, severe asthma). pH falls. Compensation by the kidneys: they excrete more H⁺ and retain HCO₃⁻ — within 3–5 days pH returns to normal.
<b>Дыхательный алкалоз</b>: гипервентиля: Respiratory alkalosis: hyperventilation (panic, high altitude, fever) “blows off” CO₂ — pH rises, and there may be cramps and numbness (ionized calcium falls). The kidneys compensate by losing HCO₃⁻.
<b>Метаболический ацидоз</b>: накопление: Metabolic acidosis: accumulation of acids (ketoacidosis in diabetes, lactate in shock, kidney failure) or loss of HCO₃⁻ (diarrhea). Compensation by the lungs: deep, labored Kussmaul breathing lowers pCO₂.
<b>Метаболический алкалоз</b>: потеря ки: Metabolic alkalosis: loss of acid (repeated vomiting of gastric juice) or excess alkali and diuretics. Compensation: breathing slows and pCO₂ rises (but not by much, since lack of oxygen gets in the way).
<b>Острое воспаление</b>: печень в ответ: Acute inflammation: in response to interleukin-6 the liver produces acute-phase proteins — α₁ (antitrypsin) and α₂ (haptoglobin, ceruloplasmin) rise, as do C-reactive protein and fibrinogen. Albumin falls slightly (a “negative acute-phase protein”).
<b>Нефротический синдром</b>: повреждённ: Nephrotic syndrome: damaged glomeruli let albumin into the urine (more than 3 g a day). Blood albumin falls sharply, and water leaves the vessels for the tissues: edema. The large α₂-macroglobulin and lipoproteins stay behind, and their share rises.
<b>Цирроз печени</b>: печень почти не си: Liver cirrhosis: the liver barely synthesizes albumin (edema, ascites), while γ-globulins rise (a polyclonal response to gut antigens that the liver no longer filters out) — the characteristic β–γ “bridge”.
<b>Миеломная болезнь</b>: опухолевый кло: Multiple myeloma: a malignant clone of plasma cells produces huge amounts of identical antibodies — a narrow, tall peak on the electrophoretogram, the M spike. Light chains (Bence Jones protein) are excreted in the urine and damage the kidneys.
<b>Гепарин</b> — сульфатированный полиса: Heparin is a sulfated polysaccharide (made by mast cells). It does not act on its own: it speeds up the natural inhibitor antithrombin III 1000-fold, which inactivates thrombin and factor Xa. It works immediately, even in a test tube; the antidote is protamine.
<b>Варфарин</b> — антагонист <b>витамина: Warfarin is a vitamin K antagonist. Vitamin K is needed by the enzyme that carboxylates glutamate residues in factors II, VII, IX and X, producing γ-carboxyglutamate (Gla), which binds Ca²⁺ and anchors the factor to the platelet membrane. Without Gla the factors do not work. It takes effect after 2–3 days and is monitored by the INR. The antidote is vitamin K.
<b>Гемофилия A</b> — наследственный (сце: Hemophilia A is an inherited (X-linked) deficiency of factor VIII. The intrinsic pathway barely works, little thrombin is made, and the fibrin mesh is loose — bleeding into joints and muscles. Treatment is replacement with factor VIII (including recombinant). Hemophilia B is a deficiency of factor IX.
<b>Аспирин</b> необратимо ацетилирует ци: Aspirin irreversibly acetylates platelet cyclooxygenase, so platelets cannot synthesize thromboxane A₂ and aggregate less well. A platelet has no nucleus and cannot make new enzyme, so the effect lasts its entire lifespan (7–10 days).
<b>Фибринолиз.</b> Когда рана зажила, тк: Fibrinolysis. Once the wound has healed, tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) converts plasminogen into plasmin, which cuts fibrin into fragments (D-dimers). tPA drugs dissolve clots in heart attack and stroke.
<b>Транексамовая кислота</b> — аналог ли: Tranexamic acid is a lysine analog: it occupies the lysine-binding sites of plasminogen, so plasminogen cannot bind to fibrin and the clot does not dissolve. It is used to treat bleeding.
Как кровь держит pH с точностью до сотых: How blood holds its pH to within hundredths, what plasma proteins carry, and how a wound seals within minutes.
\n <div><h2>Кислотно-основное состо:
Acid–base balance

  • Arterial blood pH 7.35–7.45; pCO₂ 35–45 mmHg; HCO₃⁻ 22–26 mmol/L.
  • Blood buffer capacity: hemoglobin buffer ~75%, bicarbonate ~10% (but it is “open” — regulated by the lungs and kidneys), plasma proteins, phosphates.

Plasma proteins

  • Total protein 65–85 g/L; albumin 35–50 g/L.
  • Oncotic pressure ~25 mmHg, 80% of it generated by albumin.
  • Almost all plasma proteins are synthesized by the liver, except immunoglobulins (plasma cells).

Clotting

  • Lee–White clotting time 5–10 min; prothrombin time, INR (extrinsic pathway), aPTT (intrinsic).
  • Ca²⁺ (factor IV) is needed at many steps — which is why citrate and EDTA keep donor blood from clotting in the tube.
  • Natural anticoagulants: antithrombin III, proteins C and S, tissue factor pathway inhibitor.

Models

  • IgG antibody — PDB 1IGY, factor Xa — 1IQJ (real atomic structures).
  • Albumin, transferrin and the other cascade factors are schematic “blobs”.
  • The cascade is simplified to its main steps; the rate model is qualitative.

<b>Печёночная долька</b> — шестигранная: The liver lobule is a hexagonal prism ~1 mm across: the central vein runs through the middle, and portal tracts sit at the corners (a branch of the portal vein — purple, of the hepatic artery — red, a bile duct — green). Blood from the intestine and the artery flows through sinusoids between cords of hepatocytes toward the central vein, while bile flows the opposite way, through bile canaliculi to the ducts. Everything absorbed from the intestine passes through the liver first. About 60% of liver cells are hepatocytes — the “prototype” of all cells in terms of their set of enzymes.
<b>Фаза I — микросомальное окисление.</b: Phase I — microsomal oxidation. A short electron transport chain operates in the ER membranes of hepatocytes: NADPH → flavoprotein (FAD) → cytochrome b5 → cytochrome P450. P450 is a heme monooxygenase: it inserts one atom of O₂ into the substrate (RH → R–OH), and the other goes to water. The hydrophobic substance (here benzene) gains a hydroxyl group (phenol). Phase II — conjugation: glucuronic acid (from UDP-glucuronate), sulfate (from PAPS), glutathione, an acetyl or a methyl group is attached to the OH group, producing a water-soluble conjugate that leaves in urine or bile.
<b>Обмен этанола.</b> 90–98% алкоголя ок: Ethanol metabolism. 90–98% of alcohol is oxidized in the liver: alcohol dehydrogenase (cytosol) → acetaldehyde → aldehyde dehydrogenase (mitochondria) → acetate → acetyl-CoA. Both reactions reduce NAD⁺ to NADH. At high doses MEOS joins in — cytochrome P450 2E1, which is induced in drinkers (hence “tolerance” and the liver’s increased sensitivity to poisons). The liver oxidizes only ~7–9 g of ethanol per hour (≈ 0.1–0.15 ‰ per hour), regardless of concentration. The shift in NADH/NAD⁺ inhibits gluconeogenesis (hypoglycemia) and increases lactate and fat synthesis (fatty liver).
<b>Парацетамол</b> в обычной дозе на 90%: Acetaminophen (paracetamol) at a normal dose is 90% conjugated with glucuronic acid and sulfate. 5–10% is oxidized by cytochrome P450 2E1 to the reactive NAPQI, which is immediately neutralized by glutathione (GSH). In an overdose (more than 7–10 g in an adult) conjugation is saturated, more goes to NAPQI, the glutathione store is depleted, and NAPQI binds to hepatocyte proteins (centrilobular necrosis; after 2–4 days, liver failure). The antidote is N-acetylcysteine, a source of cysteine for glutathione synthesis: it works best within the first 8–10 hours.
<b>Жировая инфильтрация</b> (стеатоз): т: Fatty infiltration (steatosis): triacylglycerols accumulate as droplets in hepatocytes when their inflow (lipolysis in diabetes and fasting, excess carbohydrates) exceeds their export in VLDL. Export requires phospholipids — a lack of lipotropic factors (methionine, choline) and of protein, as well as alcohol and poisons, disrupts VLDL synthesis.
<b>Цирроз</b> — финал хронического повре: Cirrhosis is the end stage of chronic injury (alcohol, viral hepatitis, steatohepatitis): dying hepatocytes are replaced by connective tissue, and septa divide the lobules into nodules, disrupting blood flow (portal hypertension, ascites) and every liver function: albumin and clotting factors fall, while blood ammonia (encephalopathy) and bilirubin rise.
<b>Зоны дольки</b> различаются по кислор: Lobule zones differ in oxygen and enzymes. Zone 1 (near the portal tracts) receives more O₂ — gluconeogenesis, β-oxidation and urea synthesis take place here. Zone 3 (near the central vein) is poor in oxygen and rich in cytochrome P450 and in enzymes of glycolysis and lipogenesis — which is why it is the first to suffer in acetaminophen and alcohol poisoning.
<b>Индукция.</b> Фенобарбитал, рифампици: Induction. Phenobarbital, rifampin, chronic alcohol use and smoking increase P450 synthesis, and the ER expands. Drugs are broken down faster (a higher dose is needed), and some substances are converted faster into toxic metabolites.
<b>Ингибирование.</b> Фуранокумарины гре: Inhibition. Grapefruit furanocoumarins, ketoconazole and clarithromycin block P450 3A4 — drugs broken down by it (statins, some calcium channel blockers) accumulate to toxic concentrations.
Выпито (порции по 14 г этанола) · 1 с =: Drinks (14 g of ethanol each) · 1 s = 36 min
<b>Дисульфирам</b> (тетурам) блокирует а: Disulfiram (Antabuse) blocks aldehyde dehydrogenase, so acetaldehyde accumulates: flushing, palpitations, nausea, a drop in blood pressure. People with the inactive ALDH2*2 variant (up to 40% of East Asians) react the same way.
<b>Фомепизол</b> блокирует алкогольдегид: Fomepizole blocks alcohol dehydrogenase. It is used as an antidote in methanol and ethylene glycol poisoning: alcohol dehydrogenase converts them into toxic formaldehyde/formic acid and oxalate. Ethanol itself has the same effect — it competes for the enzyme.
<b>N-ацетилцистеин</b> поставляет цистеи: N-acetylcysteine supplies cysteine, the limiting amino acid for glutathione synthesis (γ-Glu-Cys-Gly), and also binds NAPQI itself. Turn it on before glutathione falls below 30% and there will be no liver damage.
<b>Алкоголь и парацетамол</b> — опасное: Alcohol and acetaminophen are a dangerous combination: P450 2E1 is induced (more NAPQI), and glutathione is low because of poor nutrition and oxidative stress. Even a dose of 4–6 g becomes toxic.
Главная химическая фабрика тела: всё, чт: The body’s main chemical factory: everything absorbed in the intestine passes through it first — drugs, alcohol and poisons alike.
\n <div><h2>Функции печени</h2><ul>:
Liver functions

  • Regulatory and homeostatic: keeps the composition of the blood constant — glucose, proteins, lipoproteins.
  • Storage: glycogen, fat-soluble vitamins, B₁₂, iron.
  • Detoxification: oxidation, reduction, methylation, acetylation, conjugation, urea synthesis.
  • Excretory: bile (cholesterol, bile acids, bilirubin).
  • Metabolic: synthesis of 50% of the body’s proteins, all albumin and most clotting factors, ketone bodies, creatine, choline, uric acid.

Liver function tests

ALT, AST (hepatocyte damage), GGT and alkaline phosphatase (cholestasis), bilirubin, albumin and prothrombin time (synthetic function), ammonia.

Models

  • The cytochrome P450 heme is shown using real heme coordinates (1GZX); the ER proteins themselves are schematic “blobs”.
  • Alcohol kinetics: first-order absorption, zero-order oxidation ~7.5 g/h, volume of distribution 0.68 L/kg for a 70 kg person.
  • The acetaminophen model is qualitative: saturation of conjugation, consumption and recovery of glutathione.
